doc.title: Jimmy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Giants he did not play with; Dizzy as mentor; Coltrane talk
summary: Heath names Ellington and Basie, calls Dizzy his mentor, and tires of questions about Coltrane.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Of the giants, who you’ve talked about, are there any giants with whom you did not get to play?

Duke Ellington, Count Basie…Well I played with a lot of the others like Gil Evans’ Band, Thad Jones’ Band, Dizzy’s Band, of course. Dizzy’s my favorite, he’s my mentor. I think of Dizzy Gillespie everyday, like my parents. He flashes through my mind at some time during the day. Miles, not as much, but he was talented. People ask

me all the time, I got an email this morning before I came here. Somebody wants to do something about Coltrane and I said, “I’ve been talking about Coltrane for 40 years now, 43.” He passed when he was 40. Everybody’s talking about, “Well, you were with ‘Trane…” Well, yeah! Copy what’s in the other book! I said it, I’m not going to create anything new about Coltrane cause you want to create another book.
Now you can say, “Just read my book.”
Get it from the book, the book.

Yeah, cause why didn’t somebody write a book? That made me so mad! Why don’t you write a book about Milt Jackson, one of the most talented musicians ever? I guess he’s number ten, he ain’t number one; Miles is number one! (Laughs) I remember Pastor Berry used to kick Miles’ butt.
